# OrbTorrent Extensions

Extensions hook into moments in a download's life, the way checks run on a pull
request. An extension can look at a download **before it starts** and hold it
until the user decides, or act on it **after it finishes**. Its result shows in
the download's **Checks** tab in the inspector.

Extensions have their own page in OrbTorrent's main window: **Extensions**, at
the bottom of the sidebar. **Installed** shows which extensions check downloads
at each point, with each one's settings. **Activity** lists every check on
every download, and any download a check is holding. **Develop** has the switch
`orb dev` needs and the steps to build your own.

A switch at the top of **Installed** turns every extension off, for using
OrbTorrent as a plain torrent client. Nothing runs and no checks show until
it's back on, and each extension keeps its settings.

OrbTorrent ships two official extensions, built from this repository's
`extensions/` folder:

- **Fake Download Check** holds downloads that look fake, such as a film that
  contains a program.
- **VirusTotal Scan** looks up finished downloads' files on VirusTotal by their
  fingerprints.

## Guides

- [Getting started](getting-started.md): make, test and load your first extension.
- [Hooks](hooks.md): when they run, what they receive and return, and their limits.
- [API](api.md): everything `@orbtorrent/api` provides.
- [Manifest](manifest.md): every field of `package.json`.
- [Testing](testing.md): tests that run without OrbTorrent.
- [Sharing](sharing.md): `.orbext` files, and adding an official extension.
- [Security](security.md): the sandbox, permissions, and what OrbTorrent enforces.

For coding agents, every new extension has an `AGENTS.md` with the same
information in one file, and there's an Agent Skill in
[`skills/build-orbtorrent-extension`](../../skills/build-orbtorrent-extension).
[`llms.txt`](llms.txt) and [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt) hold these docs for
language models.

---

# Getting started

You need Node.js 22.13 or later and OrbTorrent.

## Make an extension

```sh
npm create @orbtorrent/extension@latest size-guard
cd size-guard
npm install
```

There are two templates:

- `before-start` (the default) holds downloads bigger than a limit you choose.
- `after-finish` sends a notification to your phone through ntfy when a
  download finishes. Choose it with
  `npm create @orbtorrent/extension@latest notify-me -- --template after-finish`.

The extension depends on [`@orbtorrent/api`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@orbtorrent/api),
which has the API and `orb`, the command-line tool its scripts use. It's MIT
licensed, so your extension can use any licence. In a clone of this repository,
`node sdk/bin/orb.js create size-guard` makes one that uses the SDK in the
clone instead.

The new folder has:

```
size-guard/
├── package.json     the manifest: hooks, permissions, settings
├── src/check.ts     the hook, named after it
├── tests/           JSON tests that run without OrbTorrent
├── assets/icon.png
├── AGENTS.md        everything in one file, for coding agents
└── README.md, CHANGELOG.md, tsconfig.json
```

## The loop

```sh
npm test          # orb test: runs tests/*.json without OrbTorrent
npm run build     # orb build: validates, type-checks and bundles into dist/
npm run lint      # orb lint: ESLint with OrbTorrent's rules
npm run dev       # orb dev: loads it into OrbTorrent and rebuilds on every save
```

`orb dev` and `orb run` need OrbTorrent open, with **Allow development
extensions** on. It's on the **Develop** tab of the **Extensions** page, in the
sidebar of OrbTorrent's main window. The first time a folder connects, OrbTorrent
asks before loading it. `npx orb doctor` checks all of this, and says what's
missing.

To try a hook on one of your downloads, list them, then run it on one:

```sh
npx orb downloads
npx orb run check --download "Name or info hash"
```

When it's ready, `npx orb install` packages it and asks OrbTorrent to install
it. OrbTorrent shows what it does and what it can reach, and installs it when
you confirm, replacing the development copy. `orb install` waits for your
answer, so a coding agent knows when it's done.

Every command takes `--json` for output a script or coding agent can read, and
exits with 1 when something's wrong.

## With a coding agent

Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI can do all of
this for you. On OrbTorrent's **Develop** tab, **Build with AI** turns what you
want the extension to do into a request to paste into your agent. It covers every
step above. Along the way, you're asked to turn on development extensions, to
allow the agent's folder, and to confirm the install.

## Next

- [Hooks](hooks.md) for when your code runs.
- [API](api.md) for reaching the network, files and storage.
- [Testing](testing.md) for faking the network in tests.

---

# Hooks

A hook is the default export of `src/<hook name>.ts`. It receives the download
and returns a result.

```ts
import { Download, Result } from "@orbtorrent/api";

export default async function check(download: Download): Promise<Result> {
  return { status: "passed", summary: "Looks like a real release" };
}
```

## When they run

| | `beforeStart` | `afterFinish` |
|---|---|---|
| Runs | Once the file list is known, before any data downloads | Once every wanted file has finished |
| Can hold the download | Yes: `failed` holds it until the user decides | No, it reports |
| File contents | No: the files don't exist yet | Yes, with `"files": "contents"` |
| Time limit | 15 s, of which 10 s of CPU | 6 h, of which 2 min of CPU |
| Memory | 512 MB | 512 MB |

**Before a download starts**, every way of adding one goes through the same gate:

- **When OrbTorrent asks before downloading:** the checks run in the
  confirmation once the file list is known, and a failed check turns the
  Download button into Download Anyway.
- **When downloads start right away:** the download is added so that the engine
  stops it the moment its file list arrives. The checks run, then OrbTorrent
  starts it, or holds it and sends a notification with **Download Anyway** and
  **Remove**.
- **When the user adds a download stopped** before its file list is known, it
  fetches its file list, stops, and is checked the same way. It stays stopped
  as the user chose, and is held only if a check fails.

**After a download finishes**, hooks run once per download. Each extension's
runs go one at a time, which suits services with rate limits. At launch,
OrbTorrent also runs them for downloads that finished while it wasn't watching,
if that was after the extension was turned on. The user can run any hook again
from the Checks tab.

## What a hook receives

```ts
interface Download {
  id: string;        // the info hash
  name: string;
  size: number;      // bytes of the wanted files
  isPrivate: boolean;
  files: { index: number; path: string; size: number; wanted: boolean }[];
}
```

`path` is relative to the download's folder, including its top folder. Hooks
never see absolute paths, trackers (which can carry a private tracker's personal
key) or other downloads.

## What it returns

```ts
interface Result {
  status: "passed" | "warning" | "failed" | "skipped";
  summary: string;   // one line in the Checks tab
  details?: string;  // markdown: paragraphs, "- " lists, **bold**, `code`, [links](https://…)
  link?: { title: string; url: string };
}
```

- **`passed`:** nothing wrong.
- **`warning`:** worth a look. The download carries on and gets a badge.
- **`failed`:** something is wrong.
  - Before it starts, this holds the download.
  - After it finishes, it sends a notification.
- **`skipped`:** the check didn't apply or couldn't run.

A hook that throws, crashes, or goes over a limit shows **Didn't finish** with
the reason. A `beforeStart` hook that doesn't finish lets the download start: a
broken extension never blocks downloads.

## Writing good results

- **Say which file and why.** For example: "Contains a program disguised as a
  video: Film.mp4.exe".
- **Use `failed` only when you're sure.** A false alarm that holds a download
  is worse than a missed warning.
- **Before a download starts, a network error means `skipped`**, not `failed`.

---

# API

Import everything from `@orbtorrent/api`. Extensions run in OrbTorrent's
sandboxed extension host, not Node.js or a browser, so this is how they reach
anything outside themselves.

## The environment

Extensions have the JavaScript language (ES2023 and newer) and these web APIs:

- `console`;
- `setTimeout`, `setInterval` and `queueMicrotask`;
- `URL` and `URLSearchParams`;
- `TextEncoder` and `TextDecoder`, UTF-8 only;
- `atob` and `btoa`;
- `crypto.randomUUID()` and `crypto.getRandomValues()`;
- `structuredClone`.

There's no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `require`, global `fetch` or DOM.
`orb build` refuses Node.js modules and says what to use instead.

## `fetch(url, init)`

An HTTPS request to a host listed in `permissions.network`.

```ts
const response = await fetch("https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files/" + sha256, {
  headers: { "x-apikey": apiKey },
});
if (response.ok) console.log(await response.json());
```

- **`init`:** `method` (GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE), `headers`, and
  `body`: text (use `JSON.stringify` for JSON) or a form from `files.formData`.
- **The response:** `status`, `ok`, `url` (after redirects), `headers.get()`,
  `text()` and `json()`.
- **Limits:** HTTPS on port 443 only, and never an address on the Mac or its
  local network. Redirects are followed only to declared hosts. Responses are
  limited to 10 MB, and each request times out after 30 s.

## `files`

These need `"files": "contents"` in `permissions`, and only work after a
download finishes.

- **`files.sha256(file)`:** the file's SHA-256 fingerprint in lowercase hex.
  OrbTorrent computes it natively, so large files are quick and don't count
  towards CPU time.
- **`files.formData({ name: "text", file: download.files[0] })`:** a multipart
  form for `fetch`. OrbTorrent streams the file from disk.

## `progress({ done, total, message })`

Updates the check's row in the Checks tab, for example "Checking 3 of 10 files…".

## `storage`

`get(key)`, `set(key, value)`, `remove(key)` and `keys()`. They store JSON
values, up to 1 MB in all. It's kept across runs and updates, and deleted with
the extension. Use it to avoid repeating work, such as lookups you've already
made.

## `getPreferenceValues()`

The extension's settings, typed from `package.json` in the generated
`orb-env.d.ts`. Every setting has a value: what the user chose, or its default,
or else `""`, `false`, or a dropdown's first option.

## `environment`

`extensionName`, `isDevelopment`, `entryPoint` and `apiVersion`.

## `sleep(milliseconds)`

Waits without using CPU time.

## Types

`Download`, `DownloadFile`, `Result`, `Status`, `Hook`, `Verify`,
`VerifyResult`, `Response`, `RequestInit` and `FormBody`.

---

# Manifest

An extension's `package.json` is npm's, with OrbTorrent's fields added.

```json
{
  "name": "virustotal",
  "title": "VirusTotal Scan",
  "description": "Checks finished downloads against about 70 antivirus engines.",
  "author": "orbtorrent",
  "icon": "icon.png",
  "hooks": [{ "name": "scan", "title": "Scan with VirusTotal", "event": "afterFinish" }],
  "permissions": { "files": "contents", "network": ["www.virustotal.com"] },
  "preferences": [
    { "name": "apiKey", "type": "password", "title": "API key", "required": true }
  ],
  "verify": "verify",
  "dependencies": { "@orbtorrent/api": "^1.0.0" }
}
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | A unique id: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. |
| `title` | yes | Shown on the Extensions page and in the Checks tab. |
| `description` | yes | One sentence on what it does. |
| `author` | yes | Your name or handle. |
| `icon` | no | A 512×512 PNG in `assets/`. |
| `version` | no | Such as `1.0.0`, shown on its page. Raise it when you share a change. |
| `hooks` | yes | `{ "name", "title", "description"?, "event" }`. `event` is `beforeStart` or `afterFinish`. The hook named `check` is the default export of `src/check.ts`. |
| `permissions.files` | no | `"contents"` to fingerprint and upload the download's files. |
| `permissions.network` | no | Exact host names, such as `"www.virustotal.com"`. |
| `preferences` | no | Settings OrbTorrent draws on the Extensions page. |
| `verify` | no | Names `src/<verify>.ts`, which checks the settings when the user presses Verify. |

## Preferences

`{ "name", "type", "title", "description"?, "required"?, "placeholder"?, "default"?, "label"?, "data"? }`

| Type | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `textfield` | text | |
| `password` | text | Kept in the macOS Keychain and hidden in logs. It can't have a default. |
| `checkbox` | true or false | `label` sits next to the box. |
| `dropdown` | text | `data` lists `{ "title", "value" }`. |

While a `required` setting is empty, the extension shows **Setup** and its
hooks are skipped. Put setup steps in `help.md`, which OrbTorrent shows next to
the settings.

## What users see

The Extensions page lists what each extension **can** do, from `hooks` and
`permissions`:

- see the names and sizes of the files in your downloads (always);
- hold a download before it starts (with a `beforeStart` hook);
- read the contents of your downloads (`"files": "contents"`);
- connect to each host in `permissions.network`.

OrbTorrent enforces the list, so ask only for what the extension needs.

---

# Testing

`orb test` runs every JSON file in `tests/` against the built hook, without
OrbTorrent. It runs the hook in a Node.js `vm` context set up like OrbTorrent's
extension host: no Node.js APIs, and every request answered from the test's
mocks. The rules and error messages match OrbTorrent's.

```json
{
  "name": "Fails a program that 12 engines flag",
  "hook": "scan",
  "preferences": { "apiKey": "test-key" },
  "download": {
    "name": "Tool 2.0",
    "files": [{ "path": "Tool 2.0/setup.exe", "size": 5000000, "sha256": "aaa…" }]
  },
  "storage": {},
  "mocks": {
    "fetch": [
      { "url": "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files/*", "status": 429, "times": 1 },
      { "url": "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files/*", "json": { "data": {} } }
    ]
  },
  "expect": { "status": "failed", "summaryIncludes": "12 of 70 engines" }
}
```

## Fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `hook` | The hook to run. Leave it out when there's only one. |
| `verify` | `true` runs the settings check with `preferences` instead. |
| `download` | `name`, `isPrivate` and `files` (`path`, `size`, `wanted`, and `sha256` for `files.sha256`). |
| `preferences` | Settings. Missing ones take their defaults. |
| `storage` | What `storage` holds before the run. |
| `mocks.fetch` | `{ url, method?, status?, json?, text?, headers?, times? }`. `*` in `url` matches any text. `times` answers that many requests before the next matching mock takes over. |
| `timeout` | Milliseconds, 10 000 unless set. |

## Expectations

| Key | Passes when |
|---|---|
| `status` | The result's status matches. |
| `summaryIncludes` | The summary includes the text, ignoring case. |
| `summaryMatches` | The summary matches the regular expression. |
| `detailsIncludes` | The details include the text. |
| `fetched` | Each URL (with `*`) was requested. |
| `throws` | The hook threw an error including the text. |
| `ok`, `messageIncludes` | For `verify`. |
| `not` | The expectation inside it fails. |

## Time

Timers run on a virtual clock: `setTimeout` and `sleep` fire as soon as nothing
else is pending, and `Date.now()` moves forward by the time waited. A hook that
waits 15 seconds between requests for a rate limit is tested in moments.

## The real thing

Node's JavaScript engine isn't JavaScriptCore, so rare differences are possible.
`orb run <hook> --download "<name>"` runs the hook in OrbTorrent itself.

---

# Sharing

## An .orbext file

`orb package` builds the extension and zips `dist/` into `<name>.orbext`, and
`orb install` also asks OrbTorrent on this Mac to install it. Opening
it on a Mac with OrbTorrent, or choosing it with **Install Extension…** on the
Extensions page, shows the install sheet:

- what the extension does, and who made it;
- "Not reviewed by OrbTorrent";
- when it runs, and what it can do.

Installing a newer version shows the same sheet, with new permissions marked
**New**. Installed extensions live in
`~/Library/Application Support/OrbTorrent/Extensions/Installed`.

An extension can't use an official extension's name. A development copy loaded
with `orb dev` can, and stands in for the official one while it's loaded.

## Official extensions

Official extensions live in this repository's `extensions/` folder. Each is an
npm workspace package, built by `make extensions` and shipped inside
OrbTorrent.app.

To change one:

1. Change its code and tests, and add a line to its `CHANGELOG.md`.
2. Run `make test-extensions`.
3. Open a pull request.

CI runs every extension's tests and lint. When a pull request changes an
extension's hooks or permissions, CI posts the difference as a comment, so the
reviewer sees first what users will be asked to allow.

---

# Security

Extensions are code from someone else running on the user's Mac. OrbTorrent
limits what that code can do, and doesn't rely on reviewing it alone.

## The extension host

- **A fresh process for every run.** Each hook runs in its own
  `orb-extension-host` process, which exits when the hook returns. Nothing
  carries over except through `storage`.
- **A strict macOS sandbox.** The helper has the App Sandbox entitlement and
  nothing else. It can't read or write files, connect to the network, or even
  look up a host name, and programs it starts inherit the same sandbox.
- **Everything goes through OrbTorrent.** Every request, file fingerprint,
  upload and storage write goes to OrbTorrent as a message, and OrbTorrent
  checks it against the extension's permissions first.
- **Limits.** OrbTorrent enforces time, CPU and memory limits, and kills a
  helper that goes over them. A `beforeStart` check that doesn't finish lets the
  download start.
- **JIT, only in the helper.** JavaScriptCore's JIT is on in the sandboxed
  helper, not in OrbTorrent itself.

## Network

- HTTPS only, on port 443, to hosts listed exactly in `permissions.network`.
- Redirects are followed only to hosts on the same list.
- A host that resolves to an address on the Mac or a local network is refused.
- There are no cookies and no shared cache.

## Settings and secrets

- **Passwords go in the Keychain.** `password` settings are stored in the macOS
  Keychain, not in a file.
- **An extension sees only its own settings.**
- **Secrets are hidden in logs.** OrbTorrent replaces them in its logs.
- **Removing an extension deletes its settings and storage.**

## Development

`orb dev` and `orb run` reach OrbTorrent through a socket at
`~/Library/Application Support/OrbTorrent/dev.sock`:

- only the user's account can open it (mode 0600, and the connecting process's
  user is checked);
- it's only there while **Allow development extensions** is on;
- OrbTorrent asks the first time each folder is loaded.
